summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analyzing Soony's confidential launch data, then building a general, adaptable agent product that rechecks the launch plan on every new data drop, surfaces contradictions, and acts on them with human approval.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses Sunday (art book overbooking, failed statue lot, game card airline offload) while the plan says all ok, and built a Python/web product with a poller, versioned store, verifier, Today/Launch/Routines UI, and a new 'ask the site' mechanism for packing, arrival and count questions. Steps 4 (Track) and 5/6 are in progress with parallel builders; the floor and routines work is finished and tests pass, but the latest api.py/floor changes are not yet committed.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhook or notification, so new drops must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256; existing files get replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, img); .env holds the token and is gitignored while .env.example is committed.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed with a Now line in PROGRESS.md; work goes on branch jonas/today-flow.
Book stock = last physical count + booked receipts (step 5) - consumption backflushed from the pack-out log (step 6); only 'Last count' is a measured value.

Silent-shipment check measured silence against the newest entry in the tracker, not the clock, so a frozen list looked fresh; the fix is to measure against the current time and reconcile status from goods receipts, shipping advices and replies.

api.py had two _MONEY regexes and the later one overrode the new one, so the cost-from-text parser was renamed; routines read only numeric cost, so text-only costs ('about EUR 16,800') would have been treated as free.
Two agents write impacts.json in different shapes, so news cases like magnet export controls never reach Today.

Floor questions use a generic model {kind, subject, last_known, token, answer} in floor.py with kinds packed/received/count; answers are stored in data/state/floor_counts.json, and the count page /count/<token> bypasses basic auth only for valid tokens.
Entire writes a checkpoint only when repo files change; the transcript is collected in .entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl and pushed with git push.
workflow: Run long builds as parallel builders with explicit file ownership and use SendMessage to relay spec changes; commit only when builders touching shared files (api.py) have reported, to avoid committing half-finished work.
Keep confidential data and findings local and gitignored; never put data values in code.
For standing permissions, the user allows small paid image-recognition calls without asking; this is recorded in the ask-before-spending memory file.
Check Docs artifact for edits by others before updating, and use artifacts only when the user asks (the user asked for a doc rather than an artifact for the Felix interview).

friction: SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN was empty at the start, blocking data access until the user supplied it.
User worried the Entire hooks had not fired; it was only that no checkpoint is made without file changes, and Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
Two builders edit the same api.py and launch_view.py, preventing a clean partial commit of the approver and half-done changes.
The image recognizer cannot read Word files, so the CPO memo (Collector's first, including game cards) is still unread.
An artifact page was published without a rendered preview, so its appearance was not verified.
The floor builder made one accidental write to the real data/state and deleted it right away.

Finish the Track builder: reconciled shipment status, silence measured against the clock, frozen-list case.
Fix the remaining audit points: rank cards by launch impact (350,000 cases at the port, deadline about 14:30), separate the impacts.json conflict, wire the approver everywhere.

Switch the remaining UI 'trucks' texts to the setting, write the README, demo script and video; hand-in at Sunday 12:00.
